title: Senior's toolkit: OpenAPI contracts
summary: Lint a contract, catch breaking changes in review, mock it before the backend exists and test a live API against it.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: OpenAPI contracts
steps.body: A contract is only useful if tools enforce it. These run on a laptop and in CI, and each one catches a different kind of mistake before a consumer does. All of them read OpenAPI 3.1.

toolkit.what: Lints an OpenAPI file: invalid structure, missing descriptions, operations without an `operationId`, plus any house rules your team writes.
flags: your rules (usually `extends: spectral:oas` plus custom ones)
exit non-zero on warnings too, not only errors
output as annotations on the pull request
toolkit.when: on every change to the contract, in CI

toolkit.what: Compares two versions of a contract and lists the changes that break existing consumers: a removed field, a new required parameter, a narrower enum.
flags: exit non-zero when a breaking change is found
the subcommand that lists every change, breaking or not
output for a pull request comment
toolkit.when: the contract gate in a pull request

toolkit.what: Serves a fake API from the contract alone, so the frontend or a partner can build before the backend exists. Requests that break the contract get a 4xx.
flags: dynamic: generate varied fake data instead of the examples

toolkit.what: Sits in front of the real backend and reports every request or response that does not match the contract.
flags: turn contract violations into error responses instead of warnings
toolkit.when: checking that the implementation really matches the spec

toolkit.what: Property-based testing from the contract: generates hundreds of valid and edge-case requests and reports 500s and responses that break the schema.
flags: run every built-in check (status codes, schema conformance, and more)

toolkit.what: Generates client SDKs or server stubs from the contract, so consumers never hand-write request types.
Queries YAML the way jq queries JSON. Handy for quick questions about a large contract.
flags: convert to JSON (then pipe to jq)

steps.prompt: Match each tool to the mistake it catches.
pairs: an operation without an `operationId` or description
a field removed that consumers still read
the backend returns a response the spec does not allow
an odd but valid input makes the API return 500
the frontend is blocked until the backend exists

steps.prompt: A partner's integration broke after Tuesday's release. The diff shows `customerId` changed from optional to `required` in the `POST /orders` request schema, and review approved it. Which check in CI would have stopped it?
options: `oasdiff breaking main-openapi.yaml openapi.yaml --fail-on ERR` on every pull request
steps.explain: Spectral judges one version on its own; the new spec is perfectly valid. Only a diff against the previous version sees that a new required field rejects requests that used to work.

steps.prompt: Fail the build on any breaking change between the contract on main and the one in this branch.
steps.explain: `oasdiff breaking` lists only consumer-breaking changes; `--fail-on ERR` turns them into a non-zero exit. `--fail-severity` is Spectral's flag, not oasdiff's.

steps.prompt: Does the tool need a running backend?
Order the contract checks in a pull request pipeline, cheapest first.
lines: Start the API in the job
also: Start the API in the job

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Put lint and a breaking-change diff on every pull request that touches the contract: they run in seconds and catch what reviewers miss. Hand partners a Prism mock on day one, and run Schemathesis against staging before a release.
